# Evidence card — Get back to it

General interruption research, not ADHD-specific. The restart marker is a design choice.

Use only these claims, within the scope stated. None of them tested this software.

- **CLM-RS-INTERRUPTION** (checked against an abstract or summary only): Interruption research in general (non-ADHD) participants suggests that a brief warning before an interruption, which gives time to prepare, is associated with faster resumption (Trafton et al., 2003). Memory-for-goals theory (Altmann & Trafton, 2002) holds that suspended goals decay and are retrieved through cues. This is adjacent cognitive evidence. It has not been tested in ADHD or with this software.
  Source: [Preparing to resume an interrupted task: effects of prospective goal encoding and retrospective rehearsal](https://doi.org/10.1016/S1071-5819(03)00023-5); [Memory for goals: an activation-based model](https://doi.org/10.1207/s15516709cog2601_2).

Full register, statuses and limitations: `evidence/claims.yaml` in the source repository. Runtime snapshot: `references/shared/runtime-evidence.md`. No claim has been reviewed by a clinician.
